Angle Bisector Ratio 2

GeometryTrianglesConstructions
Game: Drag the corners of a triangle and watch where the line from A cuts the opposite side.
How to play: Drag A, B or C with a mouse or finger, or focus a corner and use the arrow keys. Press the buttons to show names, hint lines and the extra construction.
Look for the math

The line that splits an angle in half seems to know something about the lengths of the sides. Drag a corner: the two ratios in the status line stay equal, however skew the triangle becomes.

The exact claim

If the bisector of angle A meets the opposite side at D, the page states

AB / AC = DB / DC.

That is the same statement as in the first applet. The difference is the proof: the first applet draws a line through C parallel to AD and mentions the external bisector as well, while this one builds a point E on AD. The logic test checks the printed ratio on hundreds of random triangles, including very flat ones, and also checks the first applet's external-bisector note. No error was found in the claim.

A second triangle inside the picture

Press Show extra construction. The point E sits on the line AD (sometimes beyond the side) so that angle ACB = angle ABE. Then triangles ACD and ABE are similar, because they also share the angle at A after the bisector splits it. Corresponding sides give

AB / AC = BE / DC.

An isosceles triangle closes the proof

Similarity also gives angle AEB = angle ADC. Passing to supplementary angles when E lies on the extension of AD gives angle BED = angle BDE, so triangle BDE is isosceles and BD = BE. Put this into the previous line and the claim follows. The little matching strokes on BD and BE mark that equality; the logic test verifies BD = BE over the same random triangles.

Why the three bisectors meet

Apply the ratio at each corner and multiply: every side length cancels, leaving 1. That is exactly Ceva's theorem, so the three bisectors of a triangle pass through a single point. The Hint button draws families of parallel strokes that make the ratios visible: matching pieces of the two sides are cut into equal counts.

Try dragging C until the triangle is almost flat, then press Hint and Check the ratio: the two numbers still agree.

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)
